_comment: Mutation testing of the business rules (the frontend's twin of PIT on *.business.*), killed by their unit tests (tests/unit/*-rules.test.ts, vitest.mutation.config.ts). Hard gate 95 % (break), recommendation 100 %, as revised by the project owner on 2026-11-03 (docs/quality/QUALITY_GATES.md).
testRunner_comment: The command runner, not @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner 10.0.0: under Vitest 5 that runner reported every runtime mutant 'survived' with 0 tests (only the static mutants, which reload the environment, were killed), because its in-process runs keep the dry run's provided context. The command runner starts Vitest once per mutant with __STRYKER_ACTIVE_MUTANT__ set, which the instrumented code reads (developer playbook, learnings log 2026-10-23). Return to the vitest runner with 'perTest' once a release supports Vitest 5, after checking that killed mutants report their tests.
concurrency_comment: Four mutant runs side by side (owner's CPU rule, 2026-11-08), each with one Vitest worker (vitest.mutation.config.ts): Stryker's default (cores - 1) times Vitest's own pool held the CPU at 90 %. Day to day use npm run mutation:shards (scripts/mutation-shards.mjs: one shard per module, only its tests, one CPU budget, unchanged shards skipped); this full run stays for a release and after a tooling change (docs/quality/QUALITY_GATES.md).
incremental_comment: A rerun tests only the mutants whose code or tests changed since the last run (history in reports/mutation, git-ignored; a clean checkout, as on CI, runs everything). Force a full run with --force - and ALWAYS after adding tests to kill survivors: with the command runner and coverageAnalysis off, Stryker cannot see which tests cover a mutant, so it reuses an old Survived result while the mutant code is unchanged, even if the tests changed (2026-10-24). Narrow it to the file: --mutate <file> --force.
timeout_comment: Generous timeouts (owner 2026-11-03): under load the default factor counted slow mutants as Timeout (a kill) that a re-run let survive; only a real infinite loop may time out.
